On 30 October 2023, the Council unanimously adopted United Kingdom draft S/2023/808 as resolution 2704 (2023) [VOTE]. The resolution extended the UN Verification Mission in Colombia's mandate until 31 October 2024 [OPERATIVE]. While resolution 2694 already covered Government–ELN verification, this instrument expressed willingness to consider Government–EMC monitoring and verification pending Secretary-General confirmation of a ceasefire with appropriate protocols [ADDITIONAL].

Brazil stated the resolution reflects Colombia's sovereign will and supported its total peace strategy, urging authorization of EMC verification only when sufficiently mature [BRAZIL]. Speaking for African members, Ghana welcomed the unanimous extension and supported EMC verification contingent on the Secretary-General's conditions, while pledging to encourage progress on the Ethnic Chapter for Afro-Colombian and Indigenous people [A3].

These statements share common ground regarding the conditional approach to EMC verification, both requiring maturity or specific Secretary-General protocols before such monitoring commences. Both also emphasized the importance of Colombia's sovereign priorities and the need for concrete progress on ethnic inclusion within the broader peace framework. On 30 October 2023, the Council unanimously adopted United Kingdom draft S/2023/808 as resolution 2704 (2023) [VOTE]. The resolution extended the UN Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2024 [OPERATIVE]. It expressed willingness to work with the Colombian Government on further mandate extension based on inter-party agreement [OPERATIVE]. Prior to this, resolution 2694 extended the Mission's role to monitoring the Government–ELN ceasefire [ADDITIONAL]. Resolution 2704 similarly expressed willingness to consider Government–EMC monitoring and verification once the Secretary-General confirms a ceasefire with appropriate protocols, noting his update on resolution 2694 implementation [ADDITIONAL].

Brazil, speaking via the presiding representative, affirmed the resolution reflected Colombia's sovereign will and supported its total peace strategy. Brazil urged the Council to authorize EMC ceasefire verification only when sufficiently mature [BRAZIL]. Ghana, speaking for the African members, welcomed the unanimous extension and supported EMC monitoring contingent on the Secretary-General's conditions [A3]. Both statements support the shared ground that verification of the Government–EMC ceasefire should proceed conditionally, pending the Secretary-General's confirmation of a mature ceasefire and appropriate protocols.
